newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Two more ex-Amcol directors charged.
newsitem.headline: Two more ex-Amcol directors charged.

text.p: Officials of Singapore's Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) said on Tuesday two former executive directors of trading and property-based Amcol Holdings had been charged with insider trading.

CAD officials said Ng Chee Kheong and Tang Siu Shing were charged on Monday with selling 57,000 shares while in possession of price-sensitive information regarding the operations of Funai, one of Amcol's companies.
They said Ng was charged with selling 27,000 shares on or about April 23 this year.
He was previously charged in October with conspiring to cheat Amcol over its investment of US$39.6 million in a resort project in Mauritius.

Tang, a former deputy chairman of the Construction Industry Development Board and a deputy secretary in the Ministry of Law, was charged with selling 30,000 shares on or around May 15 this year, the CAD officials said.
If convicted, both faced up to seven years' jail and/or fine of S$50,000 each.
Last Wednesday, the CAD charged former Amcol vice-chairman Chng Heng Tiu and former executive directors Kang Thian Leng and Jhonny Kesuma with failing to act honestly in their duties as directors.
According to the CAD charge sheet, a copy of which was made available to Reuters, Ng and Tang had price-sensitive information between January 9, 1995 and May 15, 1996.

It said they knew about the deteriorating relationship between Amcol and Japan's Funai Electric. Funai Electric had refused to cooperate on an audit and other affairs of Funai Electric Pte Ltd (Singapore).
Besides Amcol's cash flow problems, the charge sheet alleged they were also said to have known that:
- Funai had refused to lower its mark-up rates or transfer pricing rates on its electrical and electronic goods sold to Amcol's subsidiary Sankei.
- Funai was willing to buy Amcol's stake in Funai Singapore for only S$2.25 million instead of the S$10-S$15 million Amcol was asking.

- Funai had refused to grant Amcol subsidiary Sankei an exclusive agency agreement to distribute Funai products for three years and had refused to give a written commitment to supply and sell Funai products at 1995 levels to Sankei for two to three years.
- Amcol would inevitably lose distributorship rights to Funai products because of a legal suit by Amcol against the Japanese company.
The next hearing in the case is set for February 24.

The CAD officials said Ng was offered bail of S$30,000 on Monday. Tang provided bail of S$50,000 and had his passport impounded. Ng had already paid bail of S$50,000 on his previous charge and also had his passport impounded.
